To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neocortex provides dedicated processors for perceptually, motorically and cognitively specific information, the parahipocampal region extends the persistence of this information, the hippocampus provides an associative network that links the neocortical representations of events and places into a coherent memory of an episode, and the hippocampus and neocortex interact bidirectionally.

the hippocampal formation is a critical component of a distributed network of brain regions that is involved in the acquisition of new information, the storage of information over long periods of time, and the retrieval of information from long-term memory.
the hippocampal formation is a critical component of a cortical system for the acquisition, storage and retrieval of declarative memory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and neural basis of memory, and the role of the hippocampus in declarative memory.
the nature of declarative memory and its neural basis.
the nature of the brain's memory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hippocampal formation is involved in the processing of episodic memory.
declarative memory depends on a distributed network of neocortico-parahippocamp-hippocampal interactions.
the hippocampus plays an essential role in the formation of declarative memories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampal system is the neural basis of declarative memory.
declarative memory is a cortical hippocampal process, and that the hippocampal formation is not a memory system but a memory processor.
the brain uses a cortical hippocampal circuit for declarative memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
declarative memory is a cortical system, with the hippocampus acting as a central hub for the integration of information from many different cortical areas.
the neocortex and hippocampus are not separate systems, but rather are parts of an interconnected system for declarative memories.

declarative memory involves a distributed cortical-hippocampal circuit that encodes and retrieves memories through the re-activation of neocortically stored representations of perceptual and cognitive information.
